turns.t: Hi, come on in. Wow, you look soaked. Is it still pouring out there?
Pouring. And the parking garage was full, so I walked six blocks. I'm sorry, I'm a few minutes late.
Not at all. Sit, catch your breath. We have plenty of time today.
Thank you. I made notes, if that's okay. I didn't want to forget anything.
Please, notes are a gift. What would you like to start with?
I found a lump in my left breast, in the shower last week. I wrote down the date, and the time.
That must have been frightening. Tell me what you noticed.
It's about the size of a pea, firm, on the outer side. And it's a little tender when I press it.
Thank you. And how long do you think it has been there?
That's the thing, I really can't say. It might have been last month, or the month before. I only noticed it last week.
That's very common. These lumps are usually found by accident. Have you seen any fluid from the nipple?
No, nothing like that.
And any change in the skin, like dimpling or puckering?
No dimpling. I checked in the mirror, twice.
Good. Now, tell me about your health in general. Anything ongoing?
An underactive thyroid. That's the only thing.
And what do you take for it?
Levothyroxine. I think it's maybe 75 micrograms? I'd have to check the box.
That's fine, we can confirm it with your pharmacy. Once a day, in the morning?
Every morning, before breakfast. I'm quite strict about that one.
Wonderful. Anything else you take regularly?
The contraceptive pill, once a day, in the evening. Although, I have to be honest, I miss it some evenings.
Thank you for telling me. Is it most evenings you remember, or fewer?
I take it every day, I believe. But my diary has a few gaps, so I'm not certain.
Okay. Then let's say we're not certain, and we'll come back to it.
Is that important for the lump?
It can be, hormones play a role in how breast tissue behaves, which is why I ask.
I see. I wrote that my aunt had breast cancer. I should have said that first.
I'm glad you did. Which side of the family is your aunt on?
My mother's side. She was diagnosed in her fifties.
Thank you. Knowing that, we'll be a little more careful with you.
So what do you think this is? Please be honest.
Honestly, from your description, a small, firm, tender lump, it's most likely a benign cyst. But I won't leave it at a guess.
What do we do, then?
I'll order a breast ultrasound, so we can see exactly what it is. The scheduler will call you with an appointment.
And if it's something worse?
Then we'd know early, and we'd act. Right now, there's nothing to suggest that, so please try not to spiral.
I'll try. I keep imagining things.
I understand. I'd like to see you again next Friday, to go over the ultrasound together.
Next Friday. I'll put it in my notes. Thank you for taking time, doctor.

chief_complaint.value: I found a lump in my left breast

clinical_uncertainties.description: Patient cannot say when the breast lump began.
Patient gives the levothyroxine dose tentatively.
Pill is said to be taken daily but doses may be missed.
